title: Directories are silently ignored in ctx.actions.run arguments

labels.name: P3
labels.description: We're not considering working on this, but happy to review a PR. (No assignee)

labels.name: team-Rules-API
labels.description: API for writing rules/aspects: providers, runfiles, actions, artifacts

body:
### Description of the bug:


When you declare a directory and then attempt to use it in `ctx.actions.run`, it silently skips the argument.

### Which category does this issue belong to?


_No response_

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


https://github.com/matts1/bazel-base/tree/directory-repro

```
def my_rule(ctx):
  out = ctx.actions.declare_file("file")
  out_dir = ctx.actions.declare_directory("dir")
  args = ctx.actions.args()
  args.add_all([out, out_dir])
  ctx.actions.run(..., arguments=[args])
```

When you run with `bazel build -s`, you can see that the command it ends up invoking is `<binary> path/to/file` and it completely skips the directory argument.

Additionally, `print(args)` reveals that the args is generated correctly, but fails to translate correctly to the command-line.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


7.0.0

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse master; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


_No response_

### Is this a regression? If yes, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced.


No - I was also able to repro on 6.0.0
